key_insight: Adaptive Multi-Teacher Routing (ATR) turns data creation for universal machine-learning interatomic potentials into an uncertainty-aware selection and rejection problem, improving reliability by only keeping high-confidence pseudo-labels.
engineering_relevance: ATR offers a scalable way to build high-fidelity training data for atomistic models when exact quantum labels are too expensive, enabling more robust molecular dynamics and materials simulation workflows.
method: Calibrate multiple pretrained uMLIP teachers using a small seed set of real r²SCAN labels.
Score each structure–teacher pair with structural descriptors, teacher identity, and inter-teacher disagreement.
Accept reliable pseudo-labels and actively reject structures where no teacher is confident.
evidence_signal: With only 0.2% real r²SCAN labels for candidate structures, ATR generated 2.89 million traceable r²SCAN-level pseudo-labels and improved held-out benchmark performance and finite-temperature MD stability versus baseline controls.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and diversity of the pretrained teachers and on reliable uncertainty calibration; if teachers are biased or poorly matched to the target domain, rejection may still leave coverage gaps.
paper_title: Active rejection enables reliable generalization of universal machine-learning interatomic potentials
